title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 63 (Issue of bonus shares)

content.overview: Section 63 permits bonus shares only out of free reserves, the securities premium account, or the capital redemption reserve, and not in lieu of dividend.
content.glance: Section 63 permits bonus shares only out of free reserves, the securities premium account, or the capital redemption reserve, and not in lieu of dividend.
content.study: A bonus issue capitalises reserves; it is not a distribution of cash dividend. The company must be authorised by articles, must have made the partly paid shares fully paid if any, must not have defaulted in payment of statutory dues of employees or in debt servicing as stated in the section, and must follow the conditions prescribed. Bonus shares cannot be issued out of revaluation reserves. Once announced on the terms in s. 63, the company cannot withdraw the decision. The issue does not of itself change the relative voting proportions of holders of the same class.

examples.title: In lieu of dividend
examples.body: A resolution declaring bonus shares instead of a cash dividend already recommended is outside s. 63.

examples.title: Revaluation reserve
examples.body: A revaluation surplus is not a permitted source for bonus shares.

distinctions: Bonus issue (s. 63) capitalises reserves. Right issue (s. 62) raises fresh capital. Dividend (s. 123) distributes profits.
